title: What if the shepherd walked away?
paragraphs: What if the shepherd walked away?

No sling.
No stone.
No fallen giant.
Just silence where history should have thundered.

The valley still stretches between two armies—Israel trembling, Philistines mocking. The name Goliath still echoes like a curse, his voice slicing through courage: “Choose a man for yourselves… let him come down to me.” (1 Samuel 17:8)
But this time… no one comes.
Not even David.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

If David never faced Goliath, it wouldn’t just be a missed battle.
It would be a missed revelation.
Because the story was never about a boy and a giant.
It was about a God who delivers.
David said, “The battle is the Lord’s, and He will give you into our hand.” (1 Samuel 17:47)
Read that again.

Without that moment, Israel would still know God—but not like this.
Not as the God who uses the weak to shame the strong.
And maybe that’s where this hits you.
Because what you’re avoiding… might be your Goliath.

That conversation.
That obedience.
That step of faith you keep delaying.

If David stayed with the sheep, he would’ve stayed safe.
But he would’ve also stayed unknown.
And more than that—God’s power would’ve gone unseen through him.

But let’s go deeper.
Because even if David never fought Goliath…
Someone else would have had to.
Or Israel would fall.
And that’s the shadow pointing forward.
To another battlefield.
Another “impossible” enemy.
Sin.
Scripture says, “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
That’s not just ancient Israel.
That’s you.
That’s me.
And unlike Goliath, this enemy cannot be defeated with stones.
So God didn’t send another shepherd boy.
He sent His Son.
Jesus Christ stepped into a greater valley—not with a sling, but with a cross.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
That was the real battle.
And this time, the victory didn’t look like a giant falling.
It looked like a Savior dying.
But here’s the turning point.
Three days later… the stone moved.
Death didn’t win.
Sin didn’t win.
Jesus did.
“He is not here, for He has risen, as He said.” (Matthew 28:6)
So what if David never faced Goliath?
God’s plan would still move forward.
Because every story—every battle—was always leading to Jesus.
Now the question shifts.
What about you?

Will you keep standing on the sidelines…
Or will you trust the One who already won?
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.” (Romans 10:9)
This is your moment.
Not to pick up a stone.
But to surrender your life.
Growing almost daily.
Because your story isn’t about avoiding giants.
It’s about trusting the God who defeats them.
